title: Solar particle event of 10 September 2017 (GLE 72) seen inside the ISS Columbus module

input_data.owner: Stored and documented by the radiation dataset curation (see its provenance file); not copied here.
input_data.use: DosTel2 rows (about 100 s cadence, Columbus module): absorbed_dose_rate (uGy/h per the RadLab API documentation), latitude, longitude. The documented comparison instrument in Berger et al. 2018 is DOSTEL-2.

input_data.owner: Stored by the radiation dataset curation.
input_data.use: Independent instrument (ISS TEPC, 1 min UTC) for the same window; Berger et al. 2018 does not report TEPC numbers, so it has no documented outcome value of its own in this case.

documented_outcome.quote: Even though the event already began on 16:06 UTC on 10 September, the ISS transited through “safe” orbits until 11 September 04:30 when the first SPE protons where observed by both instruments at high southern latitudes.
documented_outcome.location: Section 3.3, PDF page 9 of the accepted manuscript

documented_outcome.quote: The dose measured on the day before the event reached the ISS was (as given in Table 4) 113.6 µGy/day for ISS-RADB and 103.7 µGy/day in DOSTEL-2. On 11 September it increased to 244.3 µGy/day for ISS-RADB and 163.8 µGy/day in DOSTEL-2.

If 10 September is taken as quiet day before the event, the additional dose due to the event was 146.2 µGy in Si as measured by the ISS-RADB sub-detector and 67.8 µGy in Si as measured by the DOSTEL-2 instrument.
documented_outcome.location: Section 3.3, PDF page 9; Table 4 (PDF page 20) titled 'Daily and SPE dose (no SAA) for ISS-RADB and DOSTEL-2 instrument'

documented_table.unit: uGy (absorbed dose in silicon, South Atlantic Anomaly contributions removed)

onset_relative_to_data: The RadLab file starts 2017-09-03T00:00. The event began at 2017-09-10 16:06 UTC and first reached the ISS at about 2017-09-11 04:30 UTC (Berger et al.), about 196.5 hours into the file. Elevated high-latitude dose continued on 12 September.

expected_product_output.rule_in_environment_hazards_json: Dose rate rises above the habitat's usual background, for example as a solar event builds.
expected_product_output.when: From the first high-latitude passes after 2017-09-11 04:30 UTC, not before 2017-09-10 16:06 UTC.
must_not: emergency: the radiation emergency rule needs symptoms; none are documented, and the documented event dose is 67.8 to 146.2 uGy in Si

a watch raised by South Atlantic Anomaly passes on the quiet days: they are part of this habitat's usual background (the file's highest DosTel2 rate, 479.5 uGy/h, is on 2017-09-06 at latitude -29.3, before the event)
expected_product_output.act_level: Not asserted. The act rule's threshold is still 'to be set by clinical review', and the source documents no shelter order or crew action for this event.
expected_product_output.trend: E14 trend deviation: 11 September daily dose above the 10 September quiet-day dose, as in Table 4.

replay_checks_derived_by_curator.note: Computed from ../../radiation/radlab_iss_2017-09_spe.csv by the case curator, not NASA numbers. Method: DosTel2 rows only; dose = sum of rate x interval to the next row, intervals over 300 s skipped; 'high latitude' = absolute latitude at least 45 deg. Timestamps carry no zone in the API; the match with Berger's UTC onset suggests UTC but the API does not state it.
replay_checks_derived_by_curator.why_not_equal_to_table_4: Table 4 removes SAA contributions with a method not given as an algorithm in the paper; this file keeps them. Tests should assert the direction and timing (11 September above 10 September, onset after 04:00 on 11 September), not equality with Table 4.

consumers.use: Radiation sensor ingest and the radiation watch warning replayed against a documented event
Baseline and trend deviation for dose rate, with SAA passes inside the baseline
Eval scenario: solar event on a station, expected watch, no emergency

is_not: Not a crew member's dose and not a documented crew action. An instrument's absorbed dose rate in silicon in one module.

berger2018.title: The Solar Particle Event on 10 September 2017 as observed onboard the International Space Station (ISS)
berger2018.authors: T. Berger, D. Matthiae, S. Burmeister, R. Rios, K. Lee, E. Semones, D. M. Hassler, N. Stoffle, C. Zeitlin (K. Lee and E. Semones: NASA Johnson Space Center)
berger2018.url_read_note: Accepted manuscript on the DLR repository (32 PDF pages); page numbers below are PDF pages of this copy. The publisher copy (https://doi.org/10.1029/2018SW001920) refused automated download (HTTP 403).
berger2018.is_nasa: NASA co-authored journal article with an NTRS record (no NTRS download); not a NASA publication
